cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to solve N-queens problem using backtracking.
Now, before continuing to the solution of the problem, let's identify what is N-queens problem now.
The Queen's puzzle was originally published in 1848.
It involves placing n queens on an n x n chessboard in such manner that no two queens can attack each
other.
We know that the Queen happens to be the most powerful piece on the chessboard, primarily because of
the freedom of the movement that it has.
So the queen can move into eight directions, as shown over here.
Now we know that a standard chessboard will be eight cross eight, but for making our problem, I'll
use 4x4.
So if we take 4x4, the problem statement is going to be like this.
So we need to place four queens on four cross four chessboard in such a manner that no two queens can
attack each other.
So if this is the 4x4, then we will have four queens and they don't have to be in the same column,
same row and same diagonal.
So how can we solve this problem?
So as you mentioned we are going to use the backtracking.
So we are going to check all possible options and eliminate the ones that is not working.
So for this we are going to use the tree representation of the backtracking also.
So here let's say we are placing the first queen in the first column.
So in the state space tree we are just going to put it like this.
So this is a root.
So as a first step we are going to put that queen one is located at the first column.
Then we are going to continue to the next option.
So we are going to place the next queen which is going to be for example let's say in the next column.
So if we put it in the next column, we see that they are not in the same row, they are not in the
same column, but they are in the same diagonal.
So Queen one can attack the Queen two so this means that this option is not a solution.
So we are going to eliminate this option.
So we are going to place the queen two to the next column which is going to be column three.
So as you can see in this case they are not in the same column and not in the same diagonal.
So we are not eliminating this option.
So this is the correct option.
Then we are going to continue to the place the third queen.
So when we place the third queen, in this case, we see that the third queen is located in the same
diagonal with the second queen.
So this option will be eliminated.
We are going to continue to the next option, so we cannot place it in the next column because we have
another queen over here.
We can place it in the fourth column.
So here again we see that it is located in the same diagonal with the second queen.
So this means that this option also will be eliminated.
So we are going to go back to the backtracking.
So we have checked it for the option of second queen is located at third column.
So this option is not working.
So this means that we are going to move the second queen to the next column, which is going to be column
of four.
So in this case we see that it is not located in the same row and column and diagonal with the first
one.
So this means that this option is valid.
We are going to continue to do to place the next queen.
So we cannot place it in the first column because we have a queen one in the first column, and we cannot
place it in the last column.
So we have a queen two in the last column, and we cannot place it in the third column, which is going
to be the same diagonal with the second queen.
So this means that we are going to place it over here in the second column.
So if you place it in the second column, we see that it works without any issue.
So this means that we can continue to place the fourth queen.
So we cannot place the fourth queen in the first and second columns and the last column.
So the only option is left with this column.
And here also we see that it can be attacked by Queen three.
So this means that this option also is not valid.
So we have to go back to all way to back and change the queen ones place.
Because if you place the queen one in the first column, all options are invalid.
So we have to change the queens ones place.
So if we change it to column two.
So here we don't have any issue.
So then we are going to continue to place the next queen.
So the next queen cannot be placed in the second column.
So we can place it in the first column.
We see that in the first column it is in the same diagonal.
So it's going to be attacked.
So this option is not valid.
So in the third column also it's not valid.
It's going to be attacked because it's located with the same diagonal with queen one.
Then we are going to continue to place it in the last column.
So in the last column we see that it's not located in the same column and row with the Queen one, and
it's not located in the same diagonal.
So this means that this option is valid.
Then we will continue to place the queen.
Three so third queen cannot be located at second column and third column and fourth column, because
at second and fourth column we have queen one and two.
And if you place it at column of three, it's going to be attacked by Queen two.
So it's obvious that we cannot place it at row of one and two because we have queens over here.
So this is the best option for Queen three.
Now if we continue placing the Queen four, it's obvious that we cannot place it first row and second
row and third row.
So we have to place it at the fourth row.
So at the third row we see that in the first column we have queen three.
In the second column we have queen one.
In third column we don't have anything.
So that's why we can go ahead and place it over here.
You see that when we place it over here it's not attacked by any queen.
So this is going to be the solution for N-queens problem in case of backtracking.
So as you can see, by checking the all possible options, we have found the final solution for N-queens
problem.
Now this is the logic behind the N-queens problem.
So in the next lecture we are going to go ahead and implement this in practice.
